title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance guidance for (1) RBAC and authentication, (2) audit logging, (3) data residency and retention, (4) Secure SDLC controls, (5) incident response security procedures, (6) compliance evidence workflows, and (7) risk & exception handling. It is intended for engineering, security, product and compliance stakeholders who design or operate production inference services.

Scope
- Applies to: Redwood hosted services, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), developer consoles and associated CI/CD pipelines.
- Excludes: third-party partner internal policies (refer to partner contracts).

1. RBAC & Authentication
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access to systems, with auditable identity and entitlement records.

Key principles:
- Role-based access (not individual ACLs) for all infra and product consoles.
- Separation of duties for deploy, release, and config-change actions.
- MFA enforced for all interactive accounts (SSO + enforced device posture for critical roles).
- Short-lived service credentials and scoped OIDC tokens for automation.

Roles & responsibilities (examples):
- security-admin: manage org-wide policies, exception approvals.
- infra-operator: manage cloud infra (Terraform applies, capacity).
- runtime-operator: manage inference runtime, kernel rollouts.
- dev: read/write non-prod resources, submit PRs for prod changes.

Implementation details and requirements (table):
| Area | Requirement | Enforcement point | Owner |
|-----|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| Identity provider | SSO (OIDC) + SCIM provisioning | Okta (or equivalent) for cloud; customer-managed IdP for Private | security/infra |
| Access model | Role definitions + attribute-based policies for tenant isolation | IAM + custom attribute rules for routing | security/eng-platform |
| Service auth | Short-lived tokens (<= 1h) and mTLS for internal RPCs | Vault + SPIFFE for mTLS cert issuance | eng-infra |
| Privilege elevation | Just-in-time (JIT) with approval workflow | Privileged access system (e.g., CyberArk / internal JIT) | security |

Onboarding & offboarding checklist:
1) Create role mappings in IdP and SCIM sync.
2) Assign least-privilege role.
3) Enroll device and enable MFA.
4) For offboarding: disable SSO, revoke sessions, rotate any service tokens, audit last actions.

2. Audit Logging
Goal: Produce tamper-evident, searchable logs for identity events, config changes, data access, and runtime exceptions.

Logging categories:
- Identity events: login, MFA, SCIM provisioning, token minting/revocation.
- Control plane ops: Terraform applies, canary rollouts, model version promotions.
- Data access: admin exports, customer data reads, bulk exports.
- Runtime events: model fallback, OOMs, request routing anomalies.

Retention and integrity:
- Audit logs retained in cold storage for 7 years (customer-facing export lifecycle) unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Immutable storage via WORM where required; logs cryptographically hashed and periodic attestation stored in control plane.

Alerting and monitoring:
- Create alerts for: failed privileged escalations (>3 in 1h), suspicious token minting, abnormal data export, and unexplained schema changes.
- Iteration cadence: weekly review of top 10 audit anomalies; monthly runbook drills.

3. Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary:
- Customer data (requests, responses, embeddings) is stored and processed only in customer-selected regions for Dedicated/Private. For hosted API, defaults to region per account settings.
- Data residency choices surfaced at account creation and persisted in billing/tenant metadata.

Retention tiers (examples):
- Session logs / short-term telemetry: 30 days (default).
- Operational traces / perf telemetry: 90 days.
- Audit logs: 7 years (or per customer contract).
- Customer-controlled datasets (uploads, private corpora): configurable by tenant; default 90 days.

Data deletion workflow (numbered):
1) Submit deletion request via Console or API with verification.
2) Verify identity and authorization.
3) Execute purge across stores (DB, object store, index) using idempotent delete jobs.
4) Record deletion event in audit log with job id.
5) Provide compliance export to customer on completion.

Cross-border transfer controls:
- For accounts requiring strict residency, replicate only to approved regions; any change requires security + legal approval and a documented data transfer assessment.

4. Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)
Objective: Integrate security early in development and enforce controls for model onboarding and runtime changes.

Mandatory controls:
- Threat modeling for any service exposing inference endpoints or persisting customer data (completed and reviewed before design freeze).
- Static analysis (SAST) and dependency scanning on all repos; block merges on high/critical findings.
- Secrets scanning and no hard-coded credentials; enforced pre-commit hooks and CI checks.
- PR requirements: tests, security checks, and at least one cross-team reviewer for infra/runtime changes.
- Model onboarding checklist: license check, quantization fingerprinting, eval suite run, performance profile, and risk assessment.

Release gating (CI/CD):
- Non-prod deploy: automated tests + SAST.
- Prod deploy: automated canary + manual security approve step for infra/runtime changes.
- Emergency hotfix: documented temporary exemptions with post-mortem and rollback plan.

5. Incident Response \u2013 Security Procedures
Purpose: Provide a coordinated, repeatable process for security incidents affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability.

Incident classification:
- Sev 1 (Security): confirmed customer data exfiltration, active compromise of control plane, or large-scale data integrity failure.
- Sev 2 (Security): unauthorized access attempt, limited scope data exposure, or significant privilege escalation attempt.

Response phases (numbered):
1) Detection & Triage: On-call pager -> incident commander (IC) assigned within 15 minutes.
2) Containment: isolate affected systems (network ACLs, revoke compromised credentials, disable affected workflows).
3) Eradication & Recovery: apply fixes, rotate keys, redeploy clean images, and validate integrity.
4) Post-incident: full postmortem within 7 business days; include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and lessons learned.

Communication guidelines:
- External communication must be coordinated by security + legal; pre-approved templates exist for different incident classes.
- Notify impacted customers within SLA windows defined in contracts and regulatory requirements.

Forensic evidence collection checklist:
- Preserve snapshots of logs (immutable copies), capture in-memory artifacts when possible, record timeline of actions, and ensure chain-of-custody for any exported evidence.

6. Compliance Evidence Workflows
Objective: Provide auditors and internal stakeholders with reliable, reproducible artifacts demonstrating control effectiveness.

Common evidence artifacts:
- RBAC exports (roles, members, SCIM logs).
- Audit log extracts for required time windows.
- Policy documents, threat models, and vulnerability scan results.
- Pipeline artifacts: signed build artifacts, SBOMs, and SCA reports.

Evidence request process (numbered):
1) Receive request via compliance portal (ticket created).
2) Validate scope and required retention period.
3) Pull artifacts from evidence store (read-only snapshot).
4) Sanitize outputs for customer-sensitive fields if required.
5) Deliver via secure transfer and record delivery in audit logs.

Evidence storage & retention:
- Canonical evidence store with strict access controls; retention aligned with audit log policy (7 years default).
- All evidence accesses produce an audit event and require justification recorded on the ticket.

7. Risk & Exceptions
Policy for exceptions:
- Exceptions to standard controls require documented risk assessments, mitigation compensating controls, and a time-bound approval.
- Approval path: service owner -> security -> legal (if data residency or contractual impact) -> executive (if > 90 days or high residual risk).

Exception lifecycle:
1) Submit exception request with technical justification and compensating controls.
2) Security performs risk review and recommends controls.
3) Legal reviews for contractual/regulatory impact.
4) Approval recorded with expiration date and monitoring requirements.

Risk register and monitoring:
- Maintain a living register for open exceptions, reviewed at monthly security reviews.
- Automated alerts for exceptions approaching expiry and for compensating-control failures.

Ownership & Contacts
- Security: security@redwood.com (primary), on-call security pager + escalation playbook.
- Eng infra: infra-owners@redwood.com.
- Privacy/legal: legal-privacy@redwood.com.
- Evidence request portal: https://portal.redwood.com/compliance (internal).

Appendix: Examples & CLI snippets
- Example: export RBAC roles (CLI):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/roles/export | jq '.' > roles-export.json
- Example: request data purge (API):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"type":"data_purge","tenant_id":"T-123"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/operations
